newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan stock market ends session lower.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan stock market ends session lower.

text.p: The Casablanca stock market ended the session on Thursday lower pulled down mainly by a drop in the market's largest capitalisation companies, brokers said.
The all-share index dropped 0.11 percent to 427.71 points compared with Wednesday's session.
Banque Commerciale du Maroc, a market blue chip, lost 10 dirhams to close at 660 dirhams.
BCM has a market capitalisation of more than 8.8 billion dirhams.
Societe Nationale d'Investissement, one of Morocco's largest private conglomerate, was traded at 585 dirhams, down three dirhams on the previous session.
One of the country's main active banks, Wafabank lost four dirhams to close at 500 dirhams.
One of reasons behind the market fall was the "wait and see feeling" of investors, a Casablanca-based stockbroker said.
"Many investors are also selling parts of their portfolio in order to participate in the privatisation of fertilisers firm Fertima," he said.
The government will float 30 percent of Fertima's capital which corresponds to a total 100,000 shares.
Subscriptions will be opened from 15 to 22 October 1996, officials said.
Main gains were registered by Morocco's largest private ONA Group. It was traded at 460 dirhams, up five dirhams compared with Wednesday's session.
The traded volume on the official market rose slightly to 26.2 million dirhams from 24.2 million dirhams on the previous session.
